Design and build production-grade Generative AI applications, LLM-powered solutions, and agentic frameworks in Python that solve real business problems at scale.
Develop intelligent agents that reason through complex workflows and automate critical enterprise processes, improving efficiency and reducing operational risk.
Deploy and manage containerized applications on OpenShift, ensuring reliable and scalable production environments.

Proven experience deploying and managing containerized applications on OpenShift.
Solid grounding in clean code practices, data structures, algorithms, and distributed systems.
Working knowledge of PostgreSQL and pgvector for relational and vector data storage.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Full-stack development experience.
Familiarity with additional agentic frameworks such as AutoGen, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, or Semantic Kernel.
Master's degree in computer science or a related field.

Join a global technology organization that gives Generative AI engineers the scale, data, and problem complexity to make a lasting impact.

Shape the direction of Generative AI adoption across a global technology organization.
Access ongoing learning and development opportunities to deepen your technical expertise.
Work with state-of-the-art AI-assisted development tools to accelerate your craft.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering
jobs.description:
About Blue J

Blue J is the leading generative AI solution for tax professionals and one of Canada's fastest-growing AI companies. Headquartered in Toronto, we're a high-growth B2B SaaS company building industry-leading tax research software that helps accountants find accurate answers to complex tax questions with greater speed and confidence, supporting workflows across compliance, advisory, training, tax writing, and more.

Backed by a $176M USD Series E funding round, we're scaling rapidly across North America and the UK while continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible with AI. By combining advanced technology with deep tax expertise, we empower tax professionals to work more efficiently, make better decisions, and deliver greater value to their clients.

A Note on Location

Primarily remote, but you must live within driving distance of our Toronto office. You’ll join us in person for every quarterly and occasionally for team get-togethers (typically 1–3 visits per quarter).

To help you get off to a great start, we bring all new team members together for their first three days of onboarding. If you’re based outside of our local commuting area, Blue J will arrange and cover your travel and accommodation.

About The Team

Blue J’s technology creates value when tax professionals can easily discover, trust, and incorporate it into their work. The Tax Pro Engagement pillar owns that experience, including onboarding, search, collaboration, account management, purchasing, integrations, and core customer workflows.

As Director of Engineering, you will set the pillar’s technical and organizational direction, lead multiple product-engineering teams, and partner with Engineering and Product leadership to shape priorities and measure customer value.

You will initially immerse yourself in our product, architecture, customers, and codebase while contributing to technical design and complex problem-solving. Over time, your focus will shift toward scaling the teams, leaders, systems, and practices supporting the pillar.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Director of Engineering that will guide the evolution of Blue J’s platform architecture and help our engineering teams deliver high quality products at speed. This role is ideal for someone who is a strong system designer, deeply experienced with building SaaS platforms, and energized by helping teams navigate technical complexity.

The ideal leader combines deep systems expertise with strong product instincts and a genuine commitment to user experience. They will champion the end user, challenge assumptions, and help identify new product possibilities that may not yet be obvious.

You will work closely with product, engineering, and research to define product direction, build reliable and scalable systems, and ensure our teams have the tools and infrastructure they need to ship confidently and frequently. This leader will coach senior engineers, help untangle difficult architectural challenges, jump into code and designs when needed, and grow a team made up of strong software engineers.

This role is designed for a technical leader who enjoys building, mentoring, and shaping the foundational platform that enables world class product development.

What You’ll Be Doing

Setting Direction

Using customer insight, product metrics, and experimentation to guide priorities, evaluate product decisions, and continuously improve the user experience
Collaborating with product and engineering leaders to define goals and priorities
Tying engineering work to measurable outcomes such as activation, adoption, engagement, conversion, retention, workflow completion, performance, and customer trust
Owning the long term vision for platform capabilities that support reliability, scalability, developer experience, and speed of delivery
Identifying focus areas to improve architecture, infrastructure, system performance, and cross team technical alignment

Enabling High Quality Delivery

Leading platform engineers to design and build foundational systems and internal tools
Going deep into architecture and designs to guide teams through ambiguity and complexity
Helping engineers make architectural tradeoffs that balance speed with long term maintainability
Ensuring projects stay on track and are communicated clearly to stakeholders
Supporting teams in shipping frequently, safely, and with high confidence, consistent with Blue J’s engineering culture

Strengthening the Engineering Organization

Coaching and developing engineers into strong system thinkers and leaders
Improving engineering practices that support quality, lean iteration, strong testing, and healthy system design
Hiring high performing engineers and engineering managers who raise the bar
Creating clarity around ownership, mandates, interfaces, and platform boundaries across pods

What You Offer Blue J

10+ years of hands-on experience designing and building heavily used customer facing SaaS products.
5+ years of engineering leadership experience, including responsibility for multiple teams or engineering managers.
Evidence that you have helped shape innovative products and technical direction in partnership with Product and Design, bringing an entrepreneurial and creative mindset rather than simply delivering against an established roadmap.
Strong architectural foundation with experience owning complex systems end-to-end - including roadmap creation, system design, implementation, and long-term evolution.
Ability to design and reason about scalable distributed systems, including performance, reliability, consistency, and cost tradeoffs.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a senior level IC when needed, especially during early context-building.
Track record of identifying critical issues, setting clear goals, and shaping the technical strategy for engineering organizations.
Experience aligning engineering, product, design, and legal research around shared outcomes and coordinated execution.
Clear communication skills with the ability to explain complex system designs to technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience guiding teams through architectural decisions, refactors, and long-term platform modernization.

Additional Experience That Would Be Valuable

Experience with product-led growth, customer activation, experimentation, conversion, engagement, or retention.
Experience building enterprise authentication, authorization, permissions, account structures, collaboration, billing, or purchasing systems.
Experience using product analytics and experimentation to guide technical and product decisions.

Technologies You Can Expect To Work With

These may evolve as our platform grows. Technologies currently in use include:

Node.js, React, TypeScript, Python
AWS, Cloudflare, Terraform
Kubernetes with ArgoCD, Docker
GitHub
PostgreSQL, ElasticSearch, Pinecone, DynamoDB, S3
Kafka, NATS

What We Offer You

A meaningful leadership role shaping the platform foundation of a fast growing company.
A mission-driven culture where your work directly advances clarity, efficiency, and accessibility in tax research.
Competitive base salary, stock options, and benefits designed to support you and your family.
Flexibility in how you work: primarily remote, with occasional travel to our Toronto office
A collaborative, ambitious, and supportive team that values innovation, respect, and fun.
The excitement of a fast-growing, well-funded company with clear momentum, and the resources to back bold initiatives.

The Core Values that Define Our Culture

We are customer-focused
We put team over self
We are pleasant and playful
We are open to better ideas
We move fast and fix things

What To Expect In The Interview Process

We anticipate a high volume of applicants for this role and are excited to grow our team. A human will review each application and get back to you as soon as possible. We appreciate your patience and look forward to connecting with you!

Interview Process

Chat with Elli, our Talent Acquisition Manager
Meet our VP of Engineering, Mario
Technical Deep Dive with an Engineering Team Member
System Design Exercise
Leadership interview with our VP of Engineering, Mario
Meet our CTO, Brett
Meet our CEO, Ben

We believe our strength is built on diversity of thought, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds and experiences to apply. We value inclusiveness and are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We strive to create an inclusive and accessible hiring experience for all candidates. If you need any accommodations during the interview process, please let us know in your application. Our team is dedicated to providing the necessary support and making reasonable adjustments to ensure a smooth process for everyone.

How We Use AI In Our Hiring Process

To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Blue J uses AI-enabled tools within our applicant tracking system to help organize applications and highlight profiles that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions.

Every application is reviewed by a member of our Talent team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans.

We use these tools to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment and we’re committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

This is a Level 6 in Blue J’s career level framework. We use levels to define the expected scope, autonomy, impact, decision-making, and experience for each role. Final compensation will be set fairly and thoughtfully based on experience, expertise, and alignment with the role’s responsibilities. While all candidates are expected to bring directly relevant experience, the top of the range is typically reserved for individuals who demonstrate exceptional depth in the role’s core competencies, a strong track record of impact in similar environments, and the ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy from day one.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Our Inference team is responsible for building and maintaining the critical systems that serve Claude to millions of users worldwide. We bring Claude to life by serving our models via the industry’s largest compute-agnostic inference deployments. We are responsible for the entire stack from intelligent request routing to fleet-wide orchestration across diverse AI accelerators.

The team has a dual mandate: maximizing compute efficiency
to reliably serve our explosive customer growth, while enabling breakthrough research
by giving our scientists the high-performance inference infrastructure they need to develop next-generation models. We tackle complex, distributed systems challenges across multiple accelerator families and emerging AI hardware running in multiple cloud platforms.

Inference systems are highly performance sensitive distributed systems. Inference serves hundreds of thousands of customers every day, and the size & span of the inference fleet requires sophisticated routing, scaling, and networking systems.

Key responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain the distributed systems that serve Claude to millions of users worldwide
Develop resilient, flexible systems that adapt in real time to real world events
Develop intelligent request routing, load balancing, and traffic management systems across thousands of accelerators
Maximize compute efficiency across the fleet by autoscaling and orchestrating production, research, and experimental workloads
Build and operate production-grade deployment pipelines for releasing new models to users
Provide high-performance inference infrastructure that enables researchers to develop next-generation models
Integrate new AI accelerator platforms and support inference for new model architectures

Minimum Qualifications

Significant software engineering experience, particularly with distributed systems
Results-oriented, with a bias towards flexibility and impact
Willingness to pick up slack, even if it goes outside your job description
Desire to learn more about machine learning systems and infrastructure
Thrive in environments where technical excellence directly drives both business results and research breakthroughs
Care about the societal impacts of your work

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with high-performance, large-scale distributed systems
Experience implementing and deploying machine learning systems at scale
Experience with load balancing, request routing, or traffic management systems
Familiarity with LLM inference optimization, batching, and caching strategies
Experience with Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure)
Proficiency in Python or Rust

Representative projects

Designing intelligent routing algorithms that optimize request distribution across many accelerators in different environments
Autoscaling our compute fleet to dynamically match supply with demand across production, research, and experimental workloads
Building production-grade deployment pipelines for releasing new models to millions of users reliably
Contributing to new inference features
Supporting inference for new model architectures
Analyzing observability data to tune performance based on real-world production workloads
Managing multi-region deployments and geographic routing for global customers

Deadline to apply:
None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California:
We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Reporting to the General Manager, we are hiring a Director, Technology to lead the evolution of Campana Systems’ technology strategy, architecture, infrastructure, and AXIS platform. In this newly created role, you will own the technology roadmap from strategy through execution, with accountability for modernization priorities, investment decisions, platform reliability, and measurable business outcomes. You will lead the Architecture and Infrastructure & Security teams, partner with the Director, Development, and establish the technical direction and capabilities needed to deliver on our product vision while supporting the customers who depend on our technology.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates across Canada, with working hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Eastern Time.

What’s in it for you

Shape a meaningful transformation . Build what comes next. You will lead experienced teams while shaping the standards, capabilities, and ways of working needed for the future. Own the technology roadmap

You will evaluate feasibility and business value, establish priorities, and work with technical teams to turn promising initiatives into measurable results.
Strengthen security and reliability.

Build and grow technical capabilities.
You will lead the Architecture and Infrastructure & Security teams, develop talent, strengthen accountability, and identify capability gaps. You will improve collaboration with Development and Product to ensure teams have the direction and support needed to execute the roadmap.
Connect technology to business priorities.

The platform modernization expertise.

The technical depth.
You bring strong expertise in enterprise architecture, APIs, integrations, data platforms, and cloud or hybrid environments, along with an understanding of infrastructure, cybersecurity, and disaster recovery. You can establish technical standards, evaluate emerging technologies, and guide decisions that strengthen platform performance, security, and scalability.
The experience driving innovation.
You have improved engineering practices and delivery performance across distributed teams, including those outside your direct reporting structure. You understand CI/CD, automation, and modern development practices, and can identify practical opportunities for AI, analytics, and business intelligence that deliver measurable value.
The business acumen.
You connect technology decisions to customer needs, financial priorities, and long-term business growth. You can evaluate investments, communicate complex trade-offs, and align senior leaders while staying close enough to the technology to challenge assumptions and guide execution.
The influence.
You develop strong technical leaders, establish accountability, and build cross-functional, cross-location collaboration. You are comfortable making difficult decisions, navigating competing priorities, and owning outcomes in an environment where you have the autonomy to shape what comes next.

Why join?

Axis Campana and Aquila are part of Constellation Software Inc., one of Canada's largest and most successful software companies and its most successful technology stock over the last 10 years [TSE: CSU].

Financial Accounting and Reporting

Job Summary
Reporting to the Scientific Director, the Manager provides operational leadership for the AGEWISE Institute and translates its scientific priorities into coordinated programs, partnerships, and deliverables. The Manager oversees day-to-day administration, research program coordination, financial planning, staff management, funding development, communications and performance reporting across the Institute’s research, implementation and education work streams.

AGEWISE brings together researchers across medicine, nursing, rehabilitation, kinesiology, engineering, fundamental and data sciences, and social sciences to advance healthy aging and translational geroscience. Its mandate connects discoveries in aging biology with clinical trials, community implementation and education to improve healthspan, function and quality of life. The Manager builds the operational infrastructure that enables this interdisciplinary work, including translational geroscience trials, research on accelerated aging after critical illness, and implementation of the AVOID frailty framework.

Job Description
Key responsibilities

1. Institute leadership, planning and governance

• Work with the Scientific Director to develop annual operational plans, budgets, milestones, and risk-management processes aligned with the Institute’s strategic priorities.
• Establish and maintain administrative systems, standard operating procedures, and a coordinated portfolio of Institute-supported activities.

• Coordinate member recruitment, engagement and collaboration across faculties, Research Excellence Clusters and external partners; organize the Institute launch, member meetings and protocol-development sessions.
• Where applicable, coordinate the approved transfer of Canadian Frailty Network programs, educational resources, digital tools, contracts and residual funds to AGEWISE.

2. Translational geroscience and research operations

• Coordinate research ethics and other required approval processes with responsible investigators and institutional offices; maintain systems to track approvals, amendments, training and reporting deadlines.
• Facilitate agreements and processes for data sharing, and secure information management with research and institutional teams.
• Support collaborative development of common data elements and core outcomes for geroscience trials, including steering-group and Delphi-process coordination.

3. Healthy-aging implementation and community partnerships

• Oversee program coordination and deliverables for the Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC) -funded AVOID Frailty implementation initiative, working with the project lead and community partners.
• Build and maintain relationships with older adults, caregivers, community organizations, healthcare partners and policymakers; support meaningful involvement throughout the research cycle.
• Coordinate connections between basic scientists, engineers, and clinician scientists to advance human-ready innovations and enable access to relevant research expertise and facilities.

4. Financial management, funding and sustainability

• Develop and monitor operating and project budgets; prepare forecasts and financial reports; track commitments, expenditures and funding restrictions with institutional finance staff.
• Coordinate grant-development activities, funding calendars, investigator submissions and supporting documentation; assist with budgets, operational plans and non-scientific proposal sections.

• Support academic, industry and philanthropic partnerships with the Scientific Director and appropriate institutional offices, including contract coordination, cost recovery and contributions to Institute operations.
• Maintain a sustainability plan and ensure timely sponsor and institutional reporting.

• Supervise Institute administrative and program staff assigned to the position, including recruitment, onboarding, work allocation, professional development and performance management.
• Coordinate trainee opportunities, interdisciplinary mentoring activities, educational modules and workshops in collaboration with faculty and existing academic programs.
• Organize symposia, policy roundtables and partner events; coordinate accessible website content, newsletters, public-facing materials, policy briefs and research communications with scientific contributors.
• Prepare and submit academic manuscripts of Institute’s projects as required

6. Evaluation, accountability and continuous improvement

• Maintain a dashboard of research, funding, collaboration, community engagement, training, and knowledge-mobilization indicators aligned with the proposal.
• Prepare annual reports and briefing materials for the Scientific Director, governance committees, institutional leadership, and funders.
• Identify operational risks, resource gaps and delays; recommend corrective actions and escalate issues requiring scientific or institutional decisions.
• Use feedback from members, staff, trainees, and community partners to improve Institute services and processes.

Qualifications and experience

• A doctoral degree (master’s degree a minimum) in health sciences or life sciences, research administration or a related discipline.
• At least five years of experience in research program management, preferably within a university, research institute, healthcare organization or multidisciplinary research network.
• Demonstrated experience managing budgets, grants or contracts, coordinating complex projects, and preparing reports for leadership and funders.
• Experience supervising staff and coordinating teams whose members work across disciplines or organizations.

Preferred assets

Reporting to the Scientific Director, the Manager provides operational leadership for the AGEWISE Institute and translates its scientific priorities into coordinated programs, partnerships, and deliverables. The Manager oversees day-to-day administration, research program coordination, financial planning, staff management, funding development, communications and performance reporting across the Institute’s research, implementation and education work streams.

AGEWISE brings together researchers across medicine, nursing, rehabilitation, kinesiology, engineering, fundamental and data sciences, and social sciences to advance healthy aging and translational geroscience. Its mandate connects discoveries in aging biology with clinical trials, community implementation and education to improve healthspan, function and quality of life. The Manager builds the operational infrastructure that enables this interdisciplinary work, including translational geroscience trials, research on accelerated aging after critical illness, and implementation of the AVOID frailty framework.

Job Description
Key responsibilities

1. Institute leadership, planning and governance

• Work with the Scientific Director to develop annual operational plans, budgets, milestones, and risk-management processes aligned with the Institute’s strategic priorities.
• Establish and maintain administrative systems, standard operating procedures, and a coordinated portfolio of Institute-supported activities.
• Provide secretariat support to the Steering Committee and community advisory board, including agendas, briefing materials, minutes and follow-up on decisions.
• Coordinate member recruitment, engagement and collaboration across faculties, Research Excellence Clusters and external partners; organize the Institute launch, member meetings and protocol-development sessions.
• Where applicable, coordinate the approved transfer of Canadian Frailty Network programs, educational resources, digital tools, contracts and residual funds to AGEWISE.

2. Translational geroscience and research operations

• Coordinate a portfolio spanning fundamental aging research, biomarkers, clinical and pragmatic trials, biomechanics, regenerative medicine, and accelerated aging in survivors of critical illness.
• Support the phased development of the proposed Clinical Trials Unit and contract research services, including feasibility planning, staffing needs, costing, workflows, and service arrangements in collaboration with existing research infrastructure.
• Work with investigators and study teams to develop projects, assess operational feasibility, coordinate participating sites, recruitment, and deliverables.
• Coordinate research ethics and other required approval processes with responsible investigators and institutional offices; maintain systems to track approvals, amendments, training and reporting deadlines.
• Facilitate agreements and processes for data sharing, and secure information management with research and institutional teams.
• Support collaborative development of common data elements and core outcomes for geroscience trials, including steering-group and Delphi-process coordination.

3. Healthy-aging implementation and community partnerships

• Oversee program coordination and deliverables for the Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC) -funded AVOID Frailty implementation initiative, working with the project lead and community partners.
• Build and maintain relationships with older adults, caregivers, community organizations, healthcare partners and policymakers; support meaningful involvement throughout the research cycle.
• Coordinate connections between basic scientists, engineers, and clinician scientists to advance human-ready innovations and enable access to relevant research expertise and facilities.

4. Financial management, funding and sustainability

• Develop and monitor operating and project budgets; prepare forecasts and financial reports; track commitments, expenditures and funding restrictions with institutional finance staff.
• Coordinate grant-development activities, funding calendars, investigator submissions and supporting documentation; assist with budgets, operational plans and non-scientific proposal sections.

• Prepare and submit academic manuscripts of Institute’s projects as required

6. Evaluation, accountability and continuous improvement

• Maintain a dashboard of research, funding, collaboration, community engagement, training, and knowledge-mobilization indicators aligned with the proposal.
• Prepare annual reports and briefing materials for the Scientific Director, governance committees, institutional leadership, and funders.
• Identify operational risks, resource gaps and delays; recommend corrective actions and escalate issues requiring scientific or institutional decisions.
• Use feedback from members, staff, trainees, and community partners to improve Institute services and processes.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Geotab ® is a global leader in IoT and connected transportation and certified “Great Place to Work™.” We are a company of diverse and talented individuals who work together to help businesses grow and succeed, and increase the safety and sustainability of our communities.
Geotab is advancing security, connecting commercial vehicles to the internet and providing web-based analytics to help customers better manage their fleets. Geotab’s open platform and Geotab Marketplace ®, offering hundreds of third-party solution options, allows both small and large businesses to automate operations by integrating vehicle data with their other data assets. Processing billions of data points a day, Geotab leverages data analytics and machine learning to improve productivity, optimize fleets through the reduction of fuel consumption, enhance driver safety and achieve strong compliance to regulatory changes.
Our team is growing and we’re looking for people who follow their passion, think differently and want to make an impact. Ours is a fast paced, ever changing environment. Geotabbers accept that challenge and are willing to take on new tasks and activities - ones that may not always be described in the initial job description. Join us for a fulfilling career with opportunities to innovate, great benefits, and our fun and inclusive work culture. Reach your full potential with Geotab. To see what it’s like to be a Geotabber, check out our blog and follow us @InsideGeotab on Instagram.

Who You Are

We are always looking for amazing talent who can contribute to our growth and deliver results! Geotab is seeking a Head of Tax & Asset Compliance who will own the solution domain that helps North American fleets meet their tax and asset compliance obligations while protecting profitability. If you love technology, and are keen to join an industry leader — we would love to hear from you!

What You'll Do

As a Head of Tax & Asset Compliance your key area of responsibility will be turning Geotab's telematics data into compliance outcomes (automated evidence, filings, and monitoring) that minimize compliance violations, fines, downtime, and administrative burden. You will need to work closely with the Tech Dev Board, Heads of Platform Domain, Heads of Segment Domain, peer Heads of Solution Domain, cross-functional domain teams (product managers, designers, product engineers), and external fleet customers.
To be successful in this role you will be a strategic leader with deep customer empathy, high adaptability, change readiness, and strong stakeholder management and communication skills. In addition, the successful candidate will have P&L literacy, commercial instinct, expertise in defining and tracking product KPIs, and the ability to operate at the intersection of business strategy, customer experience, and technical execution.

How You'll Make An Impact

Product Strategy & Vision: Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the domain, driving build/buy/partner decisions and evaluating emerging customer needs to strengthen market differentiation .
Business & Metric Ownership: Accountable for primary business KPAs (e.g., submission success rates, violations avoided) and driving adoption of compliance workflows .
Customer Value Delivery: Serve fleet operators, compliance managers, and asset owners as primary customers, defining and measuring experience metrics (adoption, time-to-value, NPS) .
Cross-Segment Alignment: Partner with Heads of Segment Domain to ensure tax and asset compliance capabilities are packaged and positioned effectively for key market segments .
Feedback Loops & Experience Quality: Establish strong feedback loops with customers, sales, and support to resolve product gaps while owning UX quality standards across all domain surfaces .
People Leadership & Coaching: Provide mentoring, career development, and performance management to cross-functional teams, identifying and coaching high-potential, next-generation leaders .
Culture & Capacity Management: Foster a high-trust, high-accountability team culture focused on customer obsession and rapid iteration while managing team capacity across discovery and delivery .
Financial Stewardship & Investment: Own the domain investment portfolio, leading annual planning for budget, headcount, and OKRs while balancing growth, quality, and capability bets .
Executive & Board Reporting: Translate board-level direction into execution plans and regularly report on domain outcomes, revenue contributions, and delivery health to executive leadership .
Cross-Domain & Platform Collaboration: Partner with Heads of Platform Domain to leverage shared infrastructure/APIs and coordinate with peer solution domains to eliminate duplication .
Community & Strategic Leadership: Participate in practitioner communities (Engineering, Product, Design) and lead board-appointed, cross-functional initiatives across domains .
Organizational Strategic Alignment: Support company-wide strategic initiatives, including AI workflow adoption, security posture, accessibility, and compliance pro grams

What You'll Bring To This Role

10+ years of experience in product management, product engineering, or related customer-facing product roles .
5+ years of senior product and people leadership with cross-functional scope and direct accountability for customer-facing business outcomes .
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent combination of education and work experience) .
Strong product leadership capability with demonstrated ability to define and execute customer-facing product strategy tied to measurable business outcomes, with P&L literacy and revenue attribution .
Cross-functional leadership experience managing teams across product management, product design, and product engineering disciplines, with proven capability in identifying and coaching high-potential leaders .
Excellent stakeholder management, change readiness, and communication skills to effectively collaborate with platform teams, segment leads, and executive leadership in evolving organizational structures .
Familiarity with modern product discovery, validation practices, and engineering practices (CI/CD, cloud-native delivery, agile), alongside the ability to redesign domain workflows around AI to compress effort.

If you got this far, we hope you're feeling excited about this role! Even if you don't feel you meet every single requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

Please note: Geotab does not accept agency resumes and is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Geotab employees.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Why Job Seekers Choose Geotab

Flex working arrangements
Baby bonus & parental leave top up program
Online learning and networking opportunities
Electric vehicle purchase incentive program
Competitive medical and dental benefits
Retirement savings program

*The above are offered to full-time permanent employees only

How We Work

At Geotab, we have adopted a flexible hybrid working model in that we have systems, functions, programs and policies in place to support both in-person and virtual work. However, you are welcomed and encouraged to come into our beautiful, safe, clean offices as often as you like. When working from home, you are required to have a reliable internet connection with at least 50mb DL/10mb UL. Virtual work is supported with cloud-based applications, collaboration tools and asynchronous working. The health and safety of employees are a top priority. We encourage work-life balance and keep the Geotab culture going strong with online social events, chat rooms and gatherings. Join us and help reshape the future of technology!
We believe that ensuring diversity is fundamental to our future growth and progress and is an integral part of our business. We believe that success happens where new ideas can flourish – in an environment that is rich in diversity and a place where people from various backgrounds can work together. We will ensure the accessibility needs of employees with disabilities are taken into account as part of performance management, career development, training and redeployment processes. If you require accommodation at any stage of the application process or want more information about our diversity and inclusion as well as accommodation policies and practices, please contact us at careers@geotab.com. Winnipeg Foundation is For Good. Forever. We help people give back to our shared community by connecting generous donors with causes they care about For Good. We are an endowment-based public foundation, so gifts are pooled and invested, and the annual earnings are distributed back to the community Forever. Founded in 1921, we are proud to be Canada's first community foundation. Our vision is ‘a Winnipeg where community life flourishes for all.’

The Opportunity

This new position will report to the Vice President, Community Impact. TWF is seeking a Director of Endow Manitoba to lead the Endow Manitoba program and related provincial initiatives that strengthen the sustainability, effectiveness, and growth of Manitoba’s community foundations.The successful incumbent will be a strategic, people-focused leader and relationship builder with strong communication, financial, analytical, project management, and decision-making skills.The Director will be accountable for the development, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of provincial capacity-building programs and ensure that Endow Manitoba remains responsive to emerging opportunities, risks funding requirements, and long-term sector needs.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $115,000 to $150,000. The successful candidate will be placed in the salary range depending on experience and qualifications

Key Responsibilities

Provide leadership for Endow Manitoba, translating strategic organizational priorities into annual plans, programs, resource allocations, performance measures, and sector outcomes.
Lead, coach, and develop the Endow Manitoba team, establishing clear accountabilities, performance expectations, decision-making authority, and a collaborative, inclusive, improvement-focused culture.
Oversee provincial capacity-building initiatives that strengthen community foundation governance, endowment development, financial sustainability, donor stewardship, strategic planning, leadership, grant-making, and organizational effectiveness.
Serve as a trusted resource to community foundation leaders, boards, senior leadership, and stakeholders on governance, sustainability, sector trends, emerging opportunities, and organizational capacity.
Develop and strengthen relationships with community foundations, governments, funders, sector organizations, community partners, and professional advisors, identifying opportunities for collaboration and collective impact.
Lead provincial engagement, learning, research, evaluation, and knowledge-sharing strategies, using evidence and sector insights to inform program development, investment priorities, and continuous improvement.
Develop and oversee administrative and grants budgets, funding agreements, contracts, resource allocation, and financial performance, ensuring effective stewardship, accountability, compliance, and sustainability.
Represent Endow Manitoba at provincial and national forums, conferences, committees, consultations, and sector events, strengthening its visibility, credibility, and influence within the philanthropic and charitable sectors.
Coordinate cross-functional initiatives and provide oversight of key programs and partnerships, identifying and addressing financial, operational, legal, partnership, privacy, and reputational risks and escalating material issues as required.

Degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Management, Rural Economic Development, Community Development, or a related discipline.
8+ years’ progressive leadership experience in the nonprofit, philanthropic, charitable, rural economic development, community development, or public sectors.
Understanding of community foundations, endowment development, philanthropy, and charitable-sector trends.
Relationship-driven leader with a community-focussed perspective and ability to mobilize teams around a shared vision.
Demonstrated experience leading strategic initiatives, partnerships, and organizational capacity-building efforts.
Experience working with boards, governance structures, volunteer leadership, and multi-stakeholder partnerships.
Proven ability to lead and manage staff, including developing teams and overseeing organizational priorities.
Strong financial understanding with demonstrated experience managing budgets, projects, resources, and complex stakeholder relationships.
Relevant community or economic development training or certification, such as EDAM Community Edge or the Ec.D. designation would be an asset.

Position Overview

The Executive Vice President of Business Strategy & Execution is responsible for leading the development, implementation, and execution of the company's overall business strategies and strategic growth initiatives. This position ensures that corporate objectives are translated into actionable business plans, measurable performance targets, and effective operational execution.

The EVP works closely with the CEO, executive leadership team, and department heads to identify business opportunities, improve organizational performance, oversee strategic initiatives, and ensure that business priorities are successfully implemented across the organization.

The ideal candidate is an experienced executive with a strong background in corporate strategy, business operations, organizational leadership, and enterprise-wide strategic execution.

Key Responsibilities

1. Corporate Business Strategy

Lead the development and implementation of the company's overall business strategy.

Establish long-term strategic priorities aligned with corporate objectives and market opportunities.

Evaluate industry trends, competitive positioning, and emerging business opportunities.

Provide strategic recommendations to the CEO and executive leadership team.

Translate corporate vision and business goals into actionable strategic initiatives.

Ensure that business strategies support sustainable growth and long-term profitability.

2. Strategic Execution and Implementation

Oversee the execution of major corporate strategies and business initiatives.

Convert strategic objectives into implementation plans, timelines, milestones, and measurable outcomes.

Coordinate with department executives to ensure effective execution of strategic priorities.

Monitor progress against strategic plans and address implementation challenges.

Establish accountability frameworks to ensure that business commitments are delivered.

Lead corrective actions when strategic initiatives fall behind established objectives.

3. Business Growth and Expansion

Identify and evaluate opportunities for business expansion, market development, and revenue growth.

Lead strategic initiatives involving new markets, business segments, products, and commercial opportunities.

Work with business development leadership to evaluate potential partnerships and growth opportunities.

Support market entry strategies and regional expansion initiatives.

Assess the commercial potential and strategic value of new business opportunities.

Develop recommendations to strengthen the company's competitive position.

4. Enterprise Performance Management

Establish enterprise-level performance objectives and strategic key performance indicators.

Monitor business performance, operational results, and progress toward corporate goals.

Review departmental performance and identify opportunities for improvement.

Present strategic performance reports and recommendations to the CEO and board of directors, as appropriate.

Ensure that business units remain aligned with corporate priorities.

Promote data-informed decision-making and organizational accountability.

5. Cross-Functional Leadership

Coordinate strategic execution across operations, finance, marketing, sales, business development, and other departments.

Work with executive leaders to resolve organizational challenges and execution barriers.

Ensure effective communication between corporate leadership and business units.

Align departmental plans, budgets, and resources with enterprise-wide priorities.

Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders to support successful strategy implementation.

6. Business Operations and Organizational Effectiveness

Oversee strategic business operations initiatives to improve organizational efficiency.

Identify operational weaknesses and implement improvement strategies.

Evaluate organizational structures, business processes, and management practices.

Support initiatives that improve productivity, cost efficiency, and resource utilization.

Establish consistent execution standards across business functions.

Encourage a performance-driven culture focused on measurable business results.

7. Financial and Resource Planning

Collaborate with finance leadership to align strategic initiatives with financial plans and budgets.

Evaluate investment requirements, resource allocation, and expected business returns.

Monitor the financial performance of major strategic initiatives.

Identify opportunities to optimize operating costs and improve resource efficiency.

Provide executive recommendations regarding strategic investments and business priorities.

8. Strategic Partnerships and Corporate Development

Oversee strategic partnership initiatives that support corporate growth objectives.

Evaluate potential alliances, joint ventures, acquisitions, and other business opportunities.

Work with legal, finance, and business development teams during strategic transaction planning.

Support negotiations with key corporate partners and external stakeholders.

Ensure that partnership initiatives align with the company's long-term business strategy.

9. Executive Leadership and Team Development

Provide strategic direction and leadership to senior management teams.

Establish clear executive responsibilities, performance expectations, and accountability standards.

Mentor department executives and strengthen organizational leadership capabilities.

Promote collaboration, transparency, and effective decision-making across the company.

Participate in executive planning sessions and board-level strategic discussions.

Support the development of future business leaders and management talent.

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Management, or a related field.

Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA) or a related discipline is preferred.

Minimum of 20 years of professional experience in corporate strategy, business operations, business management, or executive leadership.

Minimum of 10 years of senior leadership or executive management experience.

Demonstrated experience developing and executing enterprise-wide business strategies.

Strong understanding of corporate planning, financial performance, business growth, and organizational management.

The Director leads the assessment and documentation of complex, unusual, and non-routine accounting matters, recommends accounting policies and positions, and provides technical accounting guidance to corporate and site finance teams. The role is responsible for monitoring developments in accounting standards and leading the implementation of new or amended accounting standards across the Company.

This role works closely with Corporate Accounting, Consolidation, Treasury, Tax, site finance teams, Legal, Financial Systems, and the external auditors to ensure that significant transactions and accounting matters are appropriately evaluated, documented, accounted for, and disclosed.

Lead the preparation and review of quarterly and annual consolidated financial statements and disclosures in accordance with IFRS and applicable securities regulations.
Oversee the external financial reporting process, ensuring accuracy, completeness, compliance, and timely delivery.
Coordinate with Corporate Accounting, Consolidation, Tax, Treasury, Legal, and site finance teams to ensure accurate financial reporting and disclosures.
Review financial statement working papers, supporting schedules, and reconciliations to ensure consistency with consolidated financial records.
Serve as the Company's principal IFRS technical accounting expert, providing guidance on complex accounting matters and significant financial reporting judgments.
Research and assess complex and non-routine transactions, including mergers and acquisitions, financing arrangements, and corporate reorganizations.
Prepare and review technical accounting memoranda, documenting significant accounting conclusions and recommendations.
Develop and maintain IFRS accounting policies and procedures, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements and industry best practices.
Monitor changes in accounting standards and securities regulations, leading the implementation of new requirements as applicable.
Collaborate with external auditors to address significant accounting matters and support quarterly reviews and annual audits.
Provide technical accounting advice to senior management and the Audit Committee on significant financial reporting matters.
Lead, mentor, and develop the External Reporting and Technical Accounting team, ensuring high-quality deliverables, clear priorities, and timely execution.

Qualifications, Experience And Skill Requirements

University degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or another related field.
CPA designation, or equivalent, required.
Minimum 10 years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, preferably with a publicly traded, multi-jurisdictional organization or a large public accounting firm.
Experience preparing or reviewing IFRS financial statements and note disclosures for a publicly traded company.
Superior knowledge of IFRS and demonstrated experience researching and resolving complex accounting matters.
Experience preparing high-quality technical accounting memoranda and communicating accounting conclusions to senior management and external auditors.
Experience with mergers, acquisitions, dispositions, financing transactions, or other complex corporate transactions is desirable.
Experience working in a SOX environment.
Experience supporting quarterly reviews and annual external audits of a publicly traded company.
Strong analytical, research, judgment, and problem-solving skills.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
